title: Output-sensitive PCPP reduction
statement: Fix a canonical binary encoding of positive-input-length Boolean circuits whose encoding length is at least the circuit size, where size is the number of input bits plus the number of gates. An output-sensitive PCPP reduction consists of a semantic assignment of a PCPP description to each such circuit, a canonical binary encoding of the resulting packed descriptions, and a total function on binary strings that agrees with this encoding on encoded circuits. It also includes a single-tape Turing machine and a two-parameter runtime bound majorized by a polynomial in the sum of its arguments; on every input the machine produces the function’s output within that bound, using the circuit size and its generated proof length when decoding succeeds, and the input length and zero when decoding fails.
